title: Is the straight route on the box the shortest?
description: A box is thirty centimetres by twelve centimetres by twelve centimetres. The board compares the straight route of forty two centimetres with a slanted unfolding whose right triangle has sides twenty four and thirty two centimetres. Keeko's doubt is that the forty two centimetre route must be the shortest.
teaching_notes: One idea: a box unfolds in more than one way, and each unfolding gives its own straight line, so try every unfolding and keep the shortest. Watch for students who stop at the route that looks straight on the box.

source: For the 30 cm by 12 cm by 12 cm box, compare the 42 cm route
video_script.why: The child compares two routes on a box by finding the slanted length with the right triangle rule, because each unfolding gives its own straight line and they need not be equal.
video_script.substitution: box 30 cm by 12 cm by 12 cm; straight route 11 + 30 + 1 = 42 cm; slanted route is the longest side of a right triangle with sides 24 and 32; d squared = 576 + 1024 = 1600; d = 40 cm.
video_script.anchor: the box of the book with two unfoldings side by side, one with the straight route and one with the slanted line
video_script.wrong_answer: the forty two centimetre route must be the shortest, because it goes straight along
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko trusts the route that looks straight on the box; but each unfolding gives its own straight line, and the slanted one is 40 cm, shorter than 42 cm, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The slanted route of forty centimetres is shorter than forty two centimetres

final_answer.value: The slanted route of 40 cm is shorter than 42 cm
final_answer.spoken: the slanted route of forty centimetres is shorter than forty two centimetres

names.Ziva: the theorem used for the shortest path of 40 cm

hold_back: The slanted route of 40 cm is shorter than 42 cm
maths_rules: a box unfolds in more than one way; each unfolding gives its own straight line
slanted route: right triangle with sides 24 and 32; d squared = 24 x 24 + 32 x 32 = 576 + 1024 = 1600
40 cm is less than 42 cm, so the slanted route is shorter
wrong idea: the route that looks straight on the box is not always the shortest
video_script.design: One idea: try every unfolding and keep the shortest line. The two unfoldings sit side by side on the stage; the slanted line is drawn in the accent colour and the forty two centimetre route in the warning colour.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which route is shorter?

<bookmark mark='tri'/>The slanted line is the longest side of a right triangle with sides twenty four and thirty two.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The Ziva Theorem is about right triangles. It says the square of the longest side is the sum of the squares of the other two.

narration: <bookmark mark='sq'/>Step three, twenty four times twenty four is five hundred and seventy six. Thirty two times thirty two is one thousand and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='total'/>Add them, and the square of the path is one thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='root'/>The path is the square root of one thousand six hundred.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The slanted route of 40 cm is shorter than 42 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='root'/>The square root of one thousand six hundred is forty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The slanted route of forty centimetres is shorter than forty two centimetres.
